title: Writing Concerto for Cootie and Do Nothing Till You Hear From Me
summary: Cootie composed Concerto for Cootie alone and begged Duke to buy it on a bus from Boston for $25; the song later became a hit.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That's right. But 'Concerto for Cootie' was me alone.
Yeah.
And with him. He did the verse on it or something.
He did?
Yeah. But the part at the release, "Do Nothing Till You Hear From Me", was all me. Was all of my writing.
Had he ever heard you play it or anything?
No.
Had you ever played it over for him?
No.
So you wrote out the song and gave it to him, huh?
Yeah. I stood on the bus -- got right down there on the steps of the bus from Boston to New York, begging him to buy this song for $25.00.
(Laughter)
Well, what did he say? He didn't know if he was going to like it?
Yeah. A whole lot of jive. I don't know.
(Laughter)
Really?
And about the time we got to New York, he said, "Well, okay. I'll buy it."
Isn't that funny? Well, Cootie, I mean don't you think a lot of times he enjoyed himself that way, anyway?
Well, yes. He did.
He probably knew he was going to buy it anyway.
Yeah. Probably so. But I think in those days, there was a lot of things being created in the band. Because everyone would pitch in and do things.
Yeah.
But they found out the value of it. Then they stopped doing these things for nothing.
Yeah. Well, I mean, that makes sense, doesn't it?
Yeah. Uh-huh.
